$comment: source-leak.json (the PR-run gate config) is exempted here because its exemptFileBasenames entries list gate filenames verbatim — the identical self-referential class; it is itself the PR run's --config (self-exempt there). Config for THIS repo's own self-check run only (.github/workflows/self-check.yml). The actions-pinned-gate's source and tests necessarily contain the version-comment markers they enforce (`# vX.Y.Z` after a pinned SHA), exactly like the source-leak scanner's own rule definitions contain the markers it detects. The skills-drift-gate files (source, test, and reusable workflow) carry the literal gate name `skills-drift-gate`, which the source-leak SLG_PLANNING_DOC rule treats as a `drift-gate` planning-artifact marker — a self-referential false positive identical in kind to the actions-pinned-gate case. Its release-closeout companion source + workflow (skills-drift-closeout-sweep.mjs, skills-drift-closeout-sweep.yml) carry the same literal `skills-drift-gate` name — the .mjs has a real `import ... from "./skills-drift-gate.mjs"` and the .yml names the companion gate in its header prose — so they are exempted on the same basis; that name cannot be rephrased away. The push-arm ack-collector's regression test (collect-skills-acks.test.mjs) is exempted on the identical basis: it carries one IRREDUCIBLE real filename reference — it imports the gate at `../skills-drift-gate.mjs` — that cannot be rephrased; all rephraseable prose mentions were removed. The collector script itself (collect-skills-acks.sh) is NOT exempted — its only mention was prose that was reworded to drop the filename, so it stays fully scanned. The closeout sweep's TEST file is NOT exempted (it has no irreducible self-reference — its review/version markers were rephrased) so it stays fully scanned. The governance-drift-gate files (source, test, and reusable workflow) carry their own literal gate name `governance-drift-gate`, which the SLG_PLANNING_DOC rule treats as a `drift-gate` marker — the identical self-referential false positive as the skills-drift-gate case; that name cannot be rephrased away, so the three files are exempted on the same basis. Its fixtures (scripts/__fixtures__/governance-drift/**) are NOT exempted: their prose was reworded to drop the literal gate name, so they stay fully scanned. All such files — plus self-check.yml itself, which lists the skills-drift gate test paths — are exempted here by basename; consuming repos never receive this config and are unaffected. SLG_PRIVATE_ENG_REF (flags the private internal tracker leaking into public source) adds three more self-referential exemptions: the source-leak-gate's OWN tests (source-leak-gate.test.mjs, source-leak-ratchet.test.mjs) necessarily carry HIT/MISS example tokens (the private-tracker shorthand and repo-path forms) that prove the new rule matches private refs and does NOT match public ones — the markers ARE the test subject; and the truthful-attribution-gate's OWN test (truthful-attribution-gate.test.mjs) pins the gate's handling of historical commit-message records whose fixture strings (private-tracker shorthands) are irreducible test data, the identical class as the actions-pinned-gate test carrying version-comment markers. Every REPHRASEABLE private-eng-ref in the ci scripts/workflows/configs was reworded to a public-safe description (dropping the private issue number), NOT exempted. SLG_PRIVATE_REPO_REF and SLG_PRIVATE_DESIGN_PHRASE (siblings of SLG_PRIVATE_ENG_REF, flagging the bare GitHub path-form of OTHER private cinatra-ai repos — `cinatra-ai/design` etc. — and the descriptive `design repository` prose) ride the SAME source-leak-gate.test.mjs basename exemption: the test's HIT tokens (`cinatra-ai/design`, the `design repository` phrase) and MISS tokens (the load-bearing `@cinatra-ai/design` npm scope, the dispatch targets, whose REQUIRED machine forms are excused per match while every other form of the same name flags) ARE the test subject, irreducible test data. The fixture (source-leak.fixture.txt) is path-self-exempt by the gate. The release-workflow-pin-drift-gate files (source, test, and reusable workflow) carry their own literal gate name `release-workflow-pin-drift-gate`, which the SLG_PLANNING_DOC rule treats as a `drift-gate` marker — the identical self-referential false positive as the governance-drift-gate and skills-drift-gate cases; that name cannot be rephrased away, so the three files are exempted on the same basis. The test additionally carries `# vX.Y.Z` version-comment markers as IRREDUCIBLE test data (it asserts the gate parses gated vs ungated reusable-release refs `v0.1.0`/`v0.1.1`), the identical class as the actions-pinned-gate test carrying version-comment markers. Its fixtures (scripts/__fixtures__/release-workflow-pin-drift/**) are NOT exempted: their prose was reworded to drop the literal gate name, so they stay fully scanned. The thin scheduled caller (release-workflow-pin-drift-schedule.yml) carries two IRREDUCIBLE references — the job id and the `uses:` reusable-workflow path both name the gate and cannot be rephrased (all prose mentions were reworded to `release-pin drift check`) — so it is exempted on the same basis. No other basenames are added. The parity fixture corpus is skipped by prefix and lines marked source-leak-allow are exempt: planted detector test input and the engine's own rationale comments must be able to carry the phrasings the gate bans. SLG_PRIVATE_PROOFS_REF (the bare-name sibling of SLG_PRIVATE_REPO_REF, for the private twin of the public proof-image host) and the dynamic SLG_PRIVATE_REPO_PROBE / SLG_PRIVATE_REPO_PROBE_ERROR lane ride the SAME source-leak-gate.test.mjs basename exemption for the same reason: their HIT tokens (the private twin's name in both its bare and org-path forms) and MISS tokens (the PUBLIC twin, the npm scope, the deliberately excluded functional dispatch targets) ARE the test subject, irreducible test data. The probe lane adds no exemption of its own — it is off unless a token is present, and this repo's own runs pass none. No new basenames are added.
